fields.sections.0.ko: Google has launched Gemini 4 Argon, a new frontier AI model, globally. Developers and enterprises can access it via API through AI Studio and the Gemini platform, while Google AI Ultra subscribers can access it in Antigravity and Pro subscribers through the Gemini app and Search's AI Mode. Pricing is $2 per 2 million input tokens and $10 per 2 million output tokens, with cached input tokens receiving a 95% discount.
fields.sections.1.ko: Argon excels at in-depth work across diverse fields including coding, finance, law, cybersecurity, and science. Through precision in complex, multi-step tasks, it outperforms other frontier models and ranked first in the Vals Index, which measures economically critical sectors such as finance, coding, law, and tax.
fields.sections.2.ko: Google software engineers are deploying high-quality code faster than before using Argon. In the Antigravity environment, automated code submissions increased by over 35% while code rollbacks decreased to approximately one-third of previous levels. The Chrome team completed an architecture refactoring to separate 6 million lines of legacy folder structure from the 40 million-line Chromium codebase in a matter of weeks, enabling webpages to transition smoothly between tabs and panels without refresh and eliminating browser crashes in certain categories.
fields.sections.3.ko: Argon is delivering results across a broad range of fields from codebase optimization to scientific package performance improvement. Google's Agent Development Kit team used Argon to improve Python framework memory session preparation time by 40% and cold import speed by 21%, and accelerated molecular structure prediction speed of the open-source quantum chemistry package xTB by up to 2.3x and conformer search by 1.8x. Google's Gemma model achieved 2.85x inference speed improvement on A100 via vLLM, completing work that typically takes months in days.
fields.sections.4.ko: Argon shows significant improvements over previous Gemini models in spatial reasoning, mathematical precision, and visual coding, being applied to complex 3D visualization development. Through multi-agent loops using slash commands and custom skills in Antigravity, users are rapidly prototyping games, animations, and interactive environments directly renderable in the browser. Cases such as Pagoda architectural modeling, converting desk photos into games, and building complex 3D game engines are publicly available in Google AI Studio.
fields.sections.5.ko: Argon is being deployed in high-risk specialized work in law, finance, and science, with superior clarity of communication, accurate adherence to instructions, and minimization of unnecessary repetition compared to previous models. Companies and startups in the early access program are seeing results in deep document understanding, time-series data analysis, and building interactive analysis environments through Argon's advanced reasoning, multimodal capabilities, and ability to maintain strict grounding. Cases are presented including Chaco Canyon archaeological data integration, automated customer proposal generation and email dispatch, medical learning tool development, and furniture design.
fields.sections.6.ko: Argon is demonstrating real-world impact in the cybersecurity defense field. Google is expanding Fairwind Program partners to hundreds, and security company Wiz is conducting the 'Scan for Good' initiative using Argon. Through collaboration with government agencies, critical infrastructure exposure risks were proactively discovered and resolved, and cases include identifying vulnerabilities at medical institutions that protected hundreds of thousands of patient records.
fields.sections.7.ko: Argon is accelerating quantum error correction and algorithm design. Google's research team optimized AlphaQubit quantum error correction decoder with Argon, improving inference throughput by nearly 2x and advancing quantum circuit library standardization. In nuclear fusion research, more counterexamples to 'Grad's conjecture,' raised since 1967, are being discovered, providing benchmarks for stellarator simulation code validation.
fields.sections.8.ko: Argon is producing notable achievements in rare disease diagnosis. When Gamow Labs researchers used Argon to analyze the genome of a rare neonatal lung disease, it discovered chromosomal rearrangements that conventional software had missed for years, recording 57% and 52.2% accuracy on RareBench and LabBench evaluations respectively. This suggests the possibility of providing faster diagnosis to families suffering from rare diseases.
fields.caveat: This material represents Google's official position, so Argon's performance and use cases are all based on the company's own evaluation or limited data from early access program partners, and do not include results from independent third-party verification.
